In accordance with the provisions of the Act, read with the Rules made thereunder and Circulars issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”) (“the Circulars”), companies are allowed to hold Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) through video conference/other audio visual means (“VC/OAVM”) till further orders by MCA, without the physical presence of the Members at a common venue. Hence, in compliance with the Circulars, the AGM of the Company is being held through VC/OAVM.

The attendance of the Members attending the AGM through VC/OAVM will be counted for the purpose of reckoning the quorum under Section 103 of the Act.

The proceedings of the AGM shall be deemed to be conducted at the Registered Office of the Company i.e.

The proceedings of the AGM shall be deemed to be conducted at the Registered Office of the Company i.e.

‘B' Wing, Ahura Centre, 2nd Floor, Mahakali Caves Road, Andheri (East), Mumbai 400 093 which shall be the deemed venue of the AGM. Since the AGM is being held through VC/OAVM, the route map for the venue of the AGM is not required to be provided.

KFin Technologies Limited (“KFin”), the Company's Registrar and Transfer Agent (“RTA”) will provide the facility for voting through remote e-voting [hereinafter called as “e-Voting Service Provider (ESP)”], for participating at the AGM through VC/OAVM and for e-voting during the AGM.

Generally, a member entitled to attend and vote at a meeting is entitled to appoint a proxy to attend and vote on a poll instead of himself and the proxy need not be a member of the Company. Since the AGM is being held through VC/OAVM, physical attendance of Members is dispensed with and consequently, the facility for appointment of proxies is not applicable. Hence, proxy forms and attendance slips are not annexed to this Notice.

The Register of Directors and Key Managerial Personnel and their shareholding, maintained under Section 170 of the Act, the Register of Contracts or Arrangements in which the Directors are interested, maintained under Section 189 of the Act, certificate from the Company's Secretarial Auditors certifying that the Company's ESOS Schemes are being implemented in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, will be available for inspection by the Members through electronic mode during the AGM.

The aforesaid documents along with documents referred to in the AGM Notice will also be available electronically for inspection by the Members, without payment of any fees, from the date of circulation of this Notice up to the date of AGM, i.e. Monday, 17th August, 2026. Members seeking inspection of the aforementioned documents can send an email to agmutcl26@adityabirla.com with the subject line “UltraTech Cement Limited 26th AGM”.

The documents should be emailed to ultratechevoting@kfintech.com and a copy marked to evoting@kfintech.com with the subject line “UltraTech Cement Limited 26th AGM”.

50. In today's ever-changing dynamic digital landscape, security, foolproof systems and efficiency in identity

15 verification are paramount. We understand the need to protect the interests of shareholders as well as to comply with KYC standards. Digital identity verification using biometrics and digital ID document checks, help combat frauds even when individuals aren't physically present.

To counteract common spoofing attempts, we engage in capturing liveness detection and facial comparison technology.

KFin has introduced an Online Personal Verification (“OPV”)

process, based on liveness detection and document verification.

- A fully digital process, only requiring internet access and a device.

- Effectively reduces fraud for remote and unknown applicants.

- Users receive a link via email and SMS.

- Users record a video, take a selfie, and capture an image with their PAN card.

- Facial comparison ensures the user's identity matches their verified ID (PAN).

The Members at the Annual General Meetings (AGM) of the Company held on 12th August, 2020 and 11th August, 2023 had approved the re-appointment of Mrs. Rajashree Birla (DIN: 00022995) as director retiring by rotation and her continuation in office as a Non-Executive Director beyond the age of seventy five years.

In accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, Mrs. Rajashree Birla retires by rotation at the ensuing AGM and, being eligible, has offered herself for re-appointment.

Mrs. Rajashree Birla is an exemplar in the area of community initiatives and rural development.

Mrs. Birla chairs the Aditya Birla Centre for Community Initiatives and Rural Development, the Group's apex body responsible for development projects. She is also Chairperson of the Corporate Social Responsibility Committee of the Company. She oversees the social and welfare driven work across all the Group's major companies. The footprint of the Centre's work straddles over 9,000 villages, reaching out to 11 million people. The Group runs 24 hospitals. The Group reaches out to well over 100,000 students through its network of 54 formal schools and non-formal educational institutes.

Of these, girls constitute 50%. Both its hospitals as well as schools are ‘Not for Profit' institutions.

Mrs. Birla is a member of the Advisory Board, Columbia Global Center, Mumbai. She is the Chairperson of Xynteo's Vikaasa Advisory Board. She chairs FICCI - Aditya Birla CSR Centre for Excellence. Mrs. Birla serves as the Chairperson on the Habitat for Humanity India's IndiaBuilds Advisory Committee, and is an active member of the Habitat for Humanity Asia Pacific Development Council. Furthermore, she serves as a member at the Habitat for Humanity International Global Council. Alongside she is also engaged with the Breach Candy Hospital Trust.

She is the Chairperson of FICCI's first ever Expert Committee on CSR and is on the Board of BAIF Development Research Foundation, Pune, a Trustee of the Gujarat Vidyapith, and a Member of the Advisory Committee of the Mahatma Gandhi Sabarmati Ashram Memorial Trust.

As a patron of arts and culture, she is the President of the “Sangit Kala Kendra”, a Centre for performing arts, as well as the INT-ABPAA (INT Aditya Birla Performing Arts Academy).

In recognition of the exemplary work done by Mrs. Rajashree Birla, leading national and international organisations have showered accolades upon her. Among these the most outstanding one has been that of the Government of India who bestowed the ‘Padma Bhushan Award' in 2011 on Mrs. Rajashree Birla in the area of ‘Social Work'.

Most recently she was named the recipient of the ‘Lal Bahadur Shastri Award for Excellence 2024'. At the G20 EMPOWER Meet in Ahmedabad, the ‘G20 EMPOWER Award for ‘Lifetime Achievement' was conferred upon Mrs. Birla by Smt. Smriti Irani, the erstwhile Minister of Women and Child Development / Minority Affairs, Government of India. Furthermore, Mrs. Birla was named as an exemplar in Rotary International's healthcare programmes by the Hon'ble President, Smt. Droupadi Murmu.

Yet another prestigious award accorded to Mrs. Birla is BRICS ‘Living Legend and Icon for Community Excellence and Lifetime Achievement Award', at the hands of the then President of India, Mr. Ram Nath Kovind.

Additionally, for Mrs. Birla's unrelenting endeavours towards polio eradication, she was given the much coveted ‘Polio Eradication Champion Award' by the Government of India.

Likewise, the ‘Global Golden Peacock Award for CSR' was bestowed upon her by Dr. Ola Ullsten, the Former Prime Minister of Sweden in Portugal. Among other distinctive awards conferred upon Mrs. Birla include - the All-India Management Association's ‘Corporate Citizen of the Year Award', the IOD's ‘Distinguished Fellowship Award' and the ‘FICCI FLO Golden Laurel Award'. Under her exemplary leadership, the Economic Times' prestigious ‘Corporate Citizen of the Year Award' was presented twice to the Group in 2002 and 2012 and received by Mrs. Birla.

Over the years, Mrs. Birla has acquired a deep insight into the Company's business, operations and industry landscape, enabling her to provide valuable guidance and balanced judgment on key matters, and the Board is confident about her being able to function and effectively discharge her duties in an able and competent manner.

Dear Shareholders, In a global landscape defined by volatility, geopolitical tension, and accelerating technological change, FY 2025‑26 has been a milestone year for the Group. Our large manufacturing businesses have consolidated their leadership positions, our newer ventures are scaling with conviction, and our legacy consumer businesses are being reshaped for a new era of growth. Across this diverse portfolio, one force continues to anchor our progress- trust.

Trust is often viewed as an intangible asset. In reality, it is one of the most consequential forms of capital an institution can possess. In periods of uncertainty, markets can turn volatile and competitive advantages can erode. Trust, however, compounds. It enables organisations to make long-term investments when others hesitate, to navigate disruption with credibility, and to emerge stronger from periods of change.

For a group such as ours, trust extends far beyond the relationship between a company and its customers. It is reflected in the confidence of shareholders who support long-term value creation, the commitment of employees who choose to build their careers with us, the faith of partners and suppliers who invest alongside us, and the confidence of communities and governments that see us as a responsible participant in economic progress. Each of these constituencies grants an institution something invaluable: the licence to grow.

This is particularly relevant at a time when businesses are being asked to do more than deliver financial performance.

They are expected to navigate technological disruption, manage increasingly complex supply chains, create meaningful employment, steward natural resources responsibly and contribute to social progress. Meeting these expectations requires more than scale or strategy. It requires credibility built over years and, in many cases, decades.

The strength of our portfolio today reflects the cumulative effect of that credibility. It has allowed us to invest through cycles, pursue transformation with confidence and attract talent, capital, and partnerships that strengthen our competitive position.

Global Economy in 2025 The global economy maintained its trajectory through 2025 despite elevated tariffs, policy uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions. The impact of tariff measures was less severe than projections had suggested, and growth across major economies remained broadly stable.

World trade expanded faster than anticipated in 2025, as demand for AI-driven capex offset the effects of trade policy uncertainty and higher tariffs. The volume of world merchandise trade grew by 4.6%, compared to a forecast of 2.4%. For the second consecutive year, Asian economies were the largest contributors to total world trade volume growth, accounting for 3.2 percentage points of the 4.6% total - or 71% of the overall increase.

Trade in 2025 was also supported by investment in AI infrastructure, demand in emerging markets, fiscal and monetary expansion in advanced economies, and frontloading of imports in North America ahead of anticipated "reciprocal" tariffs from the United States. The outbreak of conflict in the Middle East on February 28, 2026, along with the partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz and damage to energy production facilities, introduced a supply shock to the global economy.

India in FY 2025-26: Domestic demand carries the economy forward Against a challenging global backdrop marked by US tariff escalations and mounting trade policy uncertainty, the Indian economy demonstrated remarkable resilience during FY 2025-26. Real GDP growth accelerated to 7.6%, up from 7.1% in FY 2024-25, cementing India's position as the fastest‑growing major economy globally.

This performance was underpinned by robust domestic demand, low inflation, and a broad pro-growth reform agenda. On the demand side, private consumption grew 7.7% year-on-year, supported by income tax reductions and rationalisation of GST rates.

Economic activity was broad-based. On the supply side, manufacturing gained momentum, driven by the automobile and fast-moving consumer goods sectors. The services sector benefited from demand in retail trade, hospitality, transportation, and real estate. India also made progress in containing inflation, with the headline rate averaging 2% in FY 2025-26, down from 4.7% the previous year.

India's economic prospects for FY27 carry both opportunities and risks. Growth is projected at 6.6% by RBI, marginally revised down due to the effects of the Middle East conflict, which has pushed up global energy prices and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. India nonetheless remains among the fastest-growing major economies globally.

Private consumption is expected to remain the primary driver of growth, though elevated global oil prices are likely to feed into domestic inflationary pressures. The GST rate reductions introduced in September 2025 are expected to partially offset this impact. Investment is projected to continue, supported by government capital expenditure, improved trade access through recently concluded free trade agreements, and a stable financial sector.

India's macroeconomic position, including foreign exchange reserves, a narrowing current account, and a path of fiscal consolidation, provides some buffer against external shocks.

The pace of the renewable energy transition, the credibility of fiscal policy, and the implementation of newly concluded trade agreements will be factors that determine the trajectory of growth in the coming years.

Aditya Birla Group: In our people we trust At the Aditya Birla Group, trust is built through experience.

It is earned in thousands of everyday interactions-when people are given opportunities to learn, when careers progress on merit, when leaders are accessible, when commitments are honoured, and when employees know they can depend on the organisation through moments that matter.

Over time, these experiences shape how people feel about the Group. They influence whether talented individuals choose to join us, whether they see a future with us, and whether they are willing to invest their energy and ambition here over the long term.

The progress we have made across talent, leadership, culture and employee experience during the year reflects this enduring focus.

Trust in Competence: Helping people succeed from day one The employee experience begins long before an individual settles into a role. The quality of hiring, onboarding and early support often shapes how quickly people become effective and how confidently they navigate a new environment.

During the year, we onboarded more than 11,700 employees, including over 80 senior leaders, across businesses and functions. Structured hiring and onboarding processes, clear communication and timely feedback helped create a stronger experience for candidates and new joiners alike.

We also continued to simplify the day-to-day employee experience through technology. Mobile-first onboarding and AI-enabled platforms such as AVA, which recorded more than 700,000 interactions during the year, improved accessibility, and delivered greater consistency at scale.

Capability building remains central to long-term success.

Employees are more likely to perform with confidence when they have access to the skills, knowledge and support required to succeed. Through Gyanodaya, our Global Centre for Leadership Training, and other business-led initiatives, we delivered more than 280 programmes, reaching over 8,500 employees across technical, functional, behavioural and leadership domains. Ninety-eight per cent of employees accessed digital or blended learning through the Gyanodaya Virtual Campus (GVC). In addition, an intense 3-month group-wide learning initiative, the ‘Learning Fest', engaged more than 39,000 employees, a fourfold increase over the previous year.

Managers play a critical role in shaping this experience.

Through coaching, feedback and day-to-day guidance, they influence how employees learn, grow and navigate their careers. We therefore continue to invest in strengthening leadership capability across the Group.

Trust in Growth: Building careers across

The strength of an organisation is often reflected in the opportunities it creates for its people. During the year, more than 6,400 employees moved across roles, functions, businesses or geographies. This is, by all accounts, a very significant number. These movements reflect the scale and diversity of opportunities available across the Group and reinforce our promise of A World of Opportunities.

Internal mobility also provides an important measure of organisational confidence. Of the 6,400+ movements during the year, more than 470 were across businesses. At senior leadership levels, cross-business mobility accounted for 15% of movements, strengthening leadership depth across the portfolio. Nearly 69% of senior management roles were filled through internal hiring, reflecting the quality and readiness of leadership talent developed within the Group.

These outcomes are supported by a disciplined approach to identifying and developing talent. 27% of employees form part of the Group Talent Pool. We have also built a strong pipeline of future leaders.

Our ability to attract high-quality talent continues to reflect the strength of our employer brand. Diversity hiring stood at 19% during the year, while retail businesses achieved 40% women hiring. Women's representation within the leadership cadre increased by 8%. Seventy-four per cent of new hires were below the age of 35, with Gen Z accounting for 39% of all new joiners.

The Group also received recognition across leading platforms including LinkedIn, the Top Employers Institute, Forbes and the Financial Times.

Trust in Care: Supporting people and families The employee experience extends beyond the workplace.

Health, wellbeing and support systems influence how people feel, perform and engage over the long term.

Through our health, wellbeing and insurance initiatives, we supported employees and their families in meaningful ways.

During the year, more than 8,600 counselling sessions were availed by employees, while workmen and staff accessed a further 3,100+ sessions, reflecting growing awareness and acceptance of mental wellbeing support. In parallel, over 3,400 eligible employees underwent annual health checkups, reinforcing our focus on preventive care.

These efforts are translating into measurable outcomes.

Among Mumbai-based employees, the proportion of individuals in the high-risk category, in terms of health, declined from 21% to 10%, while the low-risk category increased from 48% to 56%.

Employee sentiment continues to reflect this strong foundation. Trust in Purpose: Extending impact beyond the workplace Employees increasingly seek a sense of contribution that extends beyond their immediate roles. The Group's social initiatives provide opportunities to participate in that impact directly.

The invisible force behind visible progress

Dear Shareholders, The defining feature of the global and domestic economies in FY 2025-26 was resilience in the face of volatility. The global economy grew by 3.3% in 2025, as shifting trade policies and elevated geopolitical uncertainties were offset by hyperscale investments in artificial intelligence-led technologies, an accommodative monetary stance and fiscal support in major economies.

Risks to global growth have escalated with the West Asia war. The damage to critical energy facilities and closure of the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted supply chains, impacted global trade and exacerbated inflationary risks.

India on the fast track Despite the uncertain global environment, the Indian economy drew resilience from higher domestic consumption, policy reforms and sustained government investments in infrastructure. India maintained its momentum as the fastestgrowing major economy with gross domestic product (GDP)

expanding by 7.6% in FY 2025-26.

The West Asia war's supply-side shocks have tilted risks towards higher inflation and wider fiscal and trade deficits.

However, the external turbulence is offset by India's structural growth story. GDP growth is projected at 6.6% in FY 2026-27, led by sustained public capital expenditure, steady execution of infrastructure projects, policy buffers and domestic demand.

Building to grow Infrastructure and housing growth remain pivotal for cement sector demand. These sectors drove cement production volumes up by ~6.4% in FY 2025-26. India built over 9,300 kilometres of national highways in FY 2025-26, while the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) anchored housing demand to drive cement consumption at scale.

India is the second-largest cement producer globally, with cement demand expected to cross 620-630 MTPA by FY2029-30, driven by sustained infrastructure and housing demand.

Cement sector volumes are expected to grow 6-7% in FY 2026-27 on sustained demand from the housing and infrastructure sectors. India's ongoing infrastructure transformation has translated into a robust pipeline of projects nationwide.

The government has allocated ₹12.2 trillion to the infrastructure sector, ₹186.25 billion for PMAY-Urban and ₹549.17 billion for PMAY-Rural in FY 2026-27, which will stimulate demand.

Your Company's scale, operational efficiencies and balance sheet strength ensure that UltraTech is primed to capture these growth opportunities. UltraTech has cemented its position as a leading partner in India's growth, one that the nation trusts to reinforce infrastructure projects from Assam's Kumar Bhaskar Varma Setu to the Noida International Airport. We also take inspiration from the fact that a majority of Indians continue to rely on UltraTech products to build their dream homes.

Cresting new heights The convergence of our strategic imperatives - scale, efficiency and sustainability - resulted in a milestone FY 2025-26 for your Company, with new benchmarks achieved in our footprint, productivity and brand offerings.

During the year, we expanded cement capacities by 8 MTPA.

We also completed the integration of India Cements and Kesoram Industries' cement assets representing 26.3 MTPA of cumulative installed capacity. These acquired businesses are poised to become earnings contributors with 100% migration to the UltraTech brand being completed in March 2026, and cost and efficiency improvement underway.

From cement to building solutions As India's infrastructure story gathered momentum, our Company evolved with changing consumer needs. Cement was no longer just a product, but a key enabler of the built environment. We entered Ready Mix Concrete in 1998, launched Wall Care Putty in 2001, and introduced UltraTech Building Solutions in 2007 to support individual home builders. The Building Products Division was formalised in 2012 to offer new-age construction solutions, followed by the launch of ‘Utec by UltraTech' in 2022, a hyperlocal digital platform providing end-to-end home building solutions across India.

In 2025, our Company announced its entry into the wires and cables sector, further expanding its building solutions portfolio. The move reflected the growing demand from millions of households building, renovating, and upgrading homes, reinforcing our presence across the construction value chain.

Expansion of the wires and cables market The Indian wires and cables market, valued at USD 9.32 billion in 2024, is set for substantial growth and projected to reach USD 17.08 billion by 2032 at a CAGR of 7.94%. This surge is primarily fuelled by rapid urbanisation, infrastructure expansion and rising electrification across residential, commercial and industrial segments. Increasing investments in power transmission and distribution, renewable energy integration, metro rail networks, data centres and smart city infrastructure are driving the demand for high-quality electrical cables and wiring solutions. As construction activity expands, the wires and cables segment is emerging as a critical enabler of modern infrastructure, presenting significant opportunities for companies to expand into adjacent building material categories.

Our foray into the wires and cables segment has strengthened our building solutions portfolio. Leveraging the strength of the UltraTech brand and the reach of our distribution network, we are building market presence and positioning the Company as a comprehensive infrastructure and construction solutions provider.

Capitalising on dynamic shifts The Indian cement sector continues to witness rapid growth, driven by rapid urbanisation, sustained infrastructure investments, affordable housing initiatives and the development of industrial corridors. Construction activity has increased manifold on account of these factors and in FY 2025-26, industry volumes were projected to reach ~460-465 MMT, reporting approximately 6-7% year-on-year growth, after touching ~435 MMT cement production in FY 2025.1 Despite short-term demand fluctuations, fundamentals remain robust, supported by per capita cement consumption of ~324 kg in India, much below the global average of ~460 kg. As cities expand and new urban clusters emerge, the demand for cement and building materials is expected to remain structurally strong.

Decarbonisation pillar is broadly guided by the SBTi validated targets and aligned with the GCCA 2050 Cement and Concrete Net Zero Roadmap. Our focus on energy efficiency, clinker factor reduction, use of alternate fuel, carbon capture solutions and green power is helping us to accelerate the decarbonisation journey, in spite of growth in scale and production capacity. Through these measures the Company is on track for a 27% targeted reduction in Scope 1 CO2 intensity by 2032 from a 2017 baseline. UltraTech is currently in the advanced stages of re-validating its SBTi targets to align with a 1.5°C trajectory, reinforcing its commitment to accelerated decarbonisation and long-term net-zero ambitions.

Across energy management - we prioritise operational and energy efficiency improvements, by actively reducing specific heat and power consumption, kiln optimisation, advanced process controls and expanded waste heat recovery systems. Energy transitions are driven by scaling renewable energy within our operations, again guided by our RE100 goals. We are on track for a 85% green power share by 2030 across our operations, with a combination of renewable energy and waste heat recovery solutions. The Company has also piloted India's first industrial “on-site” RE-RTC hybrid solution in Sewagram, addressing critical barriers on round the clock availability of renewable energy.

The Company also methodically focusses on water management, with a specific focus on reducing water consumption across its operations, recharging ground water by channelizing various surface and ground water sources, commitment on zero liquid discharge and recycling water, and building specific water harvesting infrastructure to support communities and other stakeholders in the water sheds it operates in. The Company has consistently been water positive, and is setting new benchmarks internally as a result of these targeted initiatives.

By nature, cement industry is at the forefront of circular economy driven by systematic integration of waste and alternative materials utilisation within its operations. The Company has been able to process industrial, municipal, agricultural and other wastes across its operations via co-processing and other means. Strategic partnerships on utilisation of red-mud (waste generating from aluminium processing), plastics, municipal waste etc. have enabled the Company to utilise more than 49 million tonnes of waste and alternative material this year. The Company has signed a first of its kind used oil circularity partnership, the first in the sector, with one of the leading public sector oil and gas companies in India, to further enhance closed loop operations.

Nature and biodiversity Biodiversity management and nature-based solutions are an integral focus area, across our plant operations. The Company has managed to facilitate and nurture best in class Miyawaki plantations, scientific biodiversity management and ecological restoration initiatives across its key locations.

Clear roadmaps and management plans are being defined and implemented across our critical locations, to drive these initiatives in a structured manner via cross cutting efforts across manufacturing, environment, sustainability, mining and horticultural teams.

The assessment enabled a comprehensive evaluation of the key risks and opportunities impacting the Company through a systematic analysis of both external and internal factors. The findings from this process were integrated into the enterprise risk management framework, ensuring consistency with the Company's overall risk identification, assessment, and mitigation processes.

From an external perspective, the assessment considered the impact of sustainability-related issues on society and the environment. This evaluation supported a deeper understanding of the Company's environmental and social footprint and its broader responsibilities to stakeholders.

From an internal perspective, the assessment comprehensively viewed the implications of sustainability-related issues on UltraTech's financial performance, business continuity, corporate reputation, and brand value. This helped identify material risks and opportunities with potential implications for long-term performance and resilience.

This structured and systematic approach strengthens informed decision-making, supports long-term value creation, and reinforces UltraTech's commitment to sustainable, responsible, and resilient business practices.

Significance of the issue (business case):

Health and safety are critical given our manufacturing and supply chain scale. Protecting employees, contractors and communities underpins operational continuity, compliance and morale, prevents accidents and safeguards productivity. Robust systems and a strong safety culture reinforce responsible operations and long-term value creation.

We manage safety through a strong governance framework of leadership commitment, policies and structured systems. We conduct regular hazard identification, risk assessments, standard operating procedures, audits and continuous monitoring ensure compliance. Our initiatives include safety training for employees and contractors, digital incident and near-miss reporting, Virtual Reality-based modules, preventive health check-ups and emergency preparedness such as mock drills and fire safety training. Our units are certified in implementing an Integrated Management System.

We strive to reduce environmental impact while enabling low carbon construction. These products address evolving regulatory and customer expectations, reduce transition risks, and strengthen long term competitiveness by aligning business growth with climate and sustainability goals.

Significance of the issue (business case):

Energy management is critical given the energyintensive nature of cement manufacturing. It reduces operating costs, lowers emissions and improves resource efficiency, strengthening competitiveness and resilience to price volatility and transition risks while advancing resource conservation.

Our strategy maximises resource efficiency and minimises waste. We use alternative fuels and raw materials (AFR) to reduce fossil fuel and virgin resource dependence, and incorporate by-products such as fly ash and slag. We also co-process municipal solid and plastic waste. Through process optimisation, supplier collaboration and lifecycle-based design, we embed circular principles that drive cost efficiency, stewardship and long-term value.

We integrate sustainability into product design by expanding the share of blended and low-clinker cements, increasing alternative raw materials and promoting circularity. Our approach emphasises innovation, efficiency and customer engagement to deliver low-carbon solutions and reduce transition risks, supported by waste heat recovery and energy efficiency. Products with superior sustainability and performance meet customer needs while contributing to a more sustainable future.

We emphasise energy management across our energy-intensive operations and have met our EP100 commitment to double energy productivity. We drive performance through energy-efficient technologies, waste heat recovery, process optimisation, fuel diversification and greater renewable integration.

Together these lower energy intensity and emissions, mitigate cost volatility and strengthen resilience, supporting long-term competitiveness and growth.

Managing carbon is a strategic priority across our value chain. Our decarbonisation strategy rests on various strategic pillars: operational efficiency, a low-carbon portfolio, renewable energy, circularity and R&D towards net-zero concrete by 2050. We scale low-carbon products and cut our footprint through technology evaluation, pilots and partnerships with start-ups and research institutions. Effective GHG management mitigates transition and climate risks, delivers cost efficiencies, fosters innovation, strengthens brand equity, improves access to sustainable finance and positions us as a leader in India's low-carbon transition.

Customers sit at the core of every decision and innovation. We deliver superior experiences through responsive on-site support, robust service processes and seamless digital engagement, with teams guiding customers via mobile testing vans and a structured complaint-resolution mechanism. Digital transformation enables real-time visibility and faster service. We embed AI, ML, Gen AI, AR/VR and IoT to sharpen insights, automate workflows and personalise engagement, while mobile-first applications for trade and institutional customers improve speed, transparency and efficiency, driving loyalty and value.

This year, having partnered with various companies and Municipal Corporations, we have utilised 0.6 lakh tonnes of industrial waste, 4.40 lakh tonnes of Agro-waste and 20.70 lakh tonnes of MSW as alternative fuels in our kiln operations and captive power plants. This operation not only saves the amount of GHGs from getting emitted in the atmosphere but also impacts other environmental factors. Land use and biodiversity of the adjoining areas are some of the impacts mitigated by the diverting wastes from landfill.

As per EPA Municipal solid waste (https://www.epa.gov/ report-environment/wastes) are the third-largest source of human-related methane emissions in the U.S. Methane is one of several non-CO2 gases that contribute to global climate change. Methane gas is released as wastes decompose, and emissions are a function of the total amount and makeup of the wastes as well as management facility location, design, and practices. Gas emissions can be affected by recycling and changing product use. For example, increased recycling of municipal solid waste reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills while also conserving natural resources (e.g., timber, water, and minerals) and preventing pollution by reducing the need to collect new raw materials.

We have estimated that the diversion of agro and MSW waste from landfill has resulted in the avoidance of approximately 1.3* million tonnes of CO₂e emissions.

This year we have achieved 6.6% thermal substitution rate through use of Alternative fuels in our Kilns.

UltraTech collaborates with UCLA to advance cement industry decarbonisation UltraTech entered into a collaboration agreement with the Institute for Carbon Management (“ICM”) at the University of California, Los Angeles (“UCLA”) to pilot a groundbreaking new technology: the

has developed ZeroCAL technology to reduce carbon dioxide emissions from cement manufacturing. Processes based on ZeroCAL technology can eliminate nearly 98% of CO2 emissions associated with limestone calcination in cement production.

Your Company will be the first globally, to implement the ZeroCAL process at scale, representing another significant milestone towards its commitment to Net Zero goal by 2050. The front-end engineering and design of the demonstration plant at the selected unit is progressing as per schedule to enable commissioning at the earliest.

Challenge: Cement production is a major source of CO2 emissions, particularly from limestone calcination. Overcoming this without disrupting existing manufacturing processes remains a key industry challenge.

Solution: To address this, we partnered with UCLA's Institute for Carbon Management to pilot the ZeroCAL technology. This innovative process can eliminate up to 98% of emissions from limestone decomposition without relying on carbon capture as this process electrochemically converts limestone into calcium hydroxide without releasing CO2.

Impact: ZeroCAL has the potential to eliminate up to 98% of emissions from limestone decomposition. Through this collaboration, we are taking a bold step towards decarbonising cement and leading sustainable innovation globally.

Mitigation and adaptation UltraTech Cement's approach to climate action is anchored in two strategic pillars: mitigation and adaptation.

The Company has established a robust governance framework to effectively manage climate-related risks and opportunities across its operations. Comprehensive climate risk assessments have been conducted across facilities, identifying key physical perils, with extreme heat and floods emerging as the most significant.

Climate governance and strategy The Company has established a robust ESG governance framework, with Board-level oversight of climate-related and sustainability matters. Strategic direction is provided at the executive level by the Managing Director and Chief Manufacturing Officer, while the Chief Sustainability Officer, in collaboration with functional leaders, oversees implementation across the organisation. Environmental and sustainability targets are embedded within executive performance metrics to drive accountability and alignment with corporate objectives.

The Board and executive leadership provide robust oversight of sustainability and climate-related matters. Board-level committees review strategic priorities, approve sustainability frameworks and monitor progress against defined KPIs, with meetings held quarterly and on a need basis. At the executive level, performance is reviewed on a monthly basis to ensure effective implementation. These governance bodies also assess emerging business and climate risks, oversee risk management frameworks and guide mitigation strategies to enhance organisational resilience and long-term value creation.

UltraTech Cement's climate strategy and performance UltraTech's climate strategy aligns with the TCFD frameworks and is embedded within its long-term business planning.

We are committed to transitioning to a low-carbon business and is actively factoring climate-related risks and opportunities into the Company's business strategy. This is reflected in the strategic long-term plan, which integrates GHG emissions reduction with planned business growth. The Company's approach is based on a multi-pronged strategy encompassing decarbonising the energy mix, focusing on low-carbon products, and diversification of the business across the value chain of the building and construction sector. We have evaluated risks across different time horizons, which can arise on a short-term, medium-term and long-term basis.

In recent years, UltraTech Cement has undertaken comprehensive assessments of climate-related risks and opportunities, which have been systematically integrated into its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework and risk register. These assessments enable the identification and evaluation of key climate-related physical and transition risks across operations and the value chain.

Physical risks arise from both acute (event-driven) and chronic (long-term) changes in climatic patterns, which may result in damage to assets and disruptions across the Company's operations and its upstream and downstream value chain. These risks include extreme weather events such as floods, heatwaves and cyclones, as well as gradual changes in temperature and precipitation patterns affecting operational continuity, logistics and resource availability.

The Company assesses the potential impact of physical climate risks through scenario analysis to support informed risk mitigation planning and strengthen resilience across its operations, supply chain and surrounding communities.

For risks that may not be material in the short term but could intensify over the medium to long term, scenario analysis has been conducted using four Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs): RCP 8.5, RCP 6.0, RCP 4.5 and RCP 2.6.

For risks that may not be material in the short term but could intensify over the medium to long term, scenario analysis has been conducted using four Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs): RCP 8.5, RCP 6.0, RCP 4.5 and RCP 2.6.

These scenarios help evaluate the potential impacts of changes in temperature and precipitation patterns across the geographies where the Company operates, enabling proactive planning and long-term adaptation strategies.

Our assessment includes both acute and chronic physical risks:

Acute physical risks: These risks can potentially impact sales volumes owing to the disruption of business operations through interruptions in the supply chain, a rise in logistics costs, power outages, infrastructure damage and manpower shortages, among other aspects. These risks broadly include floods, cyclones and droughts.

Chronic physical risks: The potential impact of chronic risks such as variation in temperature, precipitation and water scarcity has been assessed. A few cement plant sites are located in areas with extremely high water stress, combined with a projected long-term change in precipitation patterns.

UltraTech Cement mitigates physical climate risks through a proactive and integrated approach aimed at reducing potential operational and financial impacts arising from extreme weather events. The Company undertakes site-specific physical climate risk assessments and systematically integrates identified risks into its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), business continuity planning and disaster management frameworks.

To strengthen resilience, the Company integrates climate considerations into supply chain planning. Annual and seasonal weather forecasts are factored into sourcing decisions, particularly for fuels and critical inputs, to mitigate the risk of delays or shortages. The Company maintains strategic partnerships with geographically diversified global suppliers and adopts flexible contracting mechanisms to manage supply chain volatility. To assess medium to long-term physical risks, scenario analysis has been conducted using Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP 8.5, RCP 6.0, RCP 4.5 and RCP 2.6). These scenarios evaluate the potential impact of changes in temperature and precipitation patterns across operational geographies. The insights derived support proactive risk mitigation and adaptation planning, enhancing the resilience of the Company's operations, supply chain and the communities in which it operates.

The Company has implemented adaptation initiatives to enhance resilience, including strengthening infrastructure, improving flood protection systems and safeguarding critical assets. Water risk mitigation includes rainwater harvesting, water recycling, watershed development and the use of alternative water sources. Workforce safety is ensured through heat stress management protocols, occupational health measures and emergency response systems.

Key measures include preventive maintenance of critical assets, diversification of manufacturing locations, deployment of emergency preparedness systems and adequate insurance coverage. These initiatives collectively enhance resilience and minimise disruptions and financial losses from climate-related events such as floods, cyclones and heatwaves.

The Company has formulated and implemented a series of adaptation measures based on the outcomes of its climate risk assessments. As part of its forward-looking resilience strategy, the Company plans to undertake comprehensive physical climate risk assessments across all existing, newly acquired and upcoming facilities over the next five years.

These assessments will evaluate site-specific risks based on hazard exposure, asset vulnerability and potential impact, enabling the development of tailored adaptation plans for each location.

Following an initial risk screening exercise, Gujarat Cement Works has undergone a detailed physical climate risk assessment. This assessment identified key climate risk perils relevant to the site, evaluated their potential impacts on operations and assets, and informed the development of a site-specific adaptation plan. Based on this analysis, targeted risk mitigation and adaptation measures have been formulated to enhance the resilience of the facility against identified climate hazards.

This structured, phased approach enables the Company to systematically strengthen climate resilience across its portfolio, while integrating climate considerations into longterm capital planning and operational decision-making.

UltraTech has operationalised a 7.5 MW round-the-clock (RTC) hybrid renewable energy project at our integrated cement manufacturing unit, Sewagram Cement Works, located in Gujarat. This innovative solution integrates solar, using bifacial modules with trackers, and wind energy alongside battery storage, co-located on-site, to provide uninterrupted energy during the cement manufacturing process without any reliance on grid power. The project was executed in collaboration with clean energy solutions company Gentari.

Installed as a behind-the-meter system, the project marks the country's first in industrial power consumption and showcases what advanced system integration can achieve in terms of emissions reduction and energy cost optimisation at scale. The project, which has been executed with the objective of providing uninterrupted clean energy, represents a new benchmark in India's clean energy transition, demonstrating the power of customer-led design and integrated system engineering.

As we scale, our responsibility only grows. Our focus remains on delivering measurable outcomes, strengthening resilience, and ensuring that UltraTech continues to lead the transition towards sustainable construction.

Integration into enterprise risk management and long-term planning We incorporate biodiversity impacts into our sustainability governance framework and enterprise risk management.

Our progressive and post-closure rehabilitation strategies encompass habitat restoration and native species regeneration, with all actions aligned with regulatory requirements and our commitment to No Net Loss.

Commitment to biodiversity conservation We are committed to implementing best-practice and sitespecific measures to protect biodiversity and manage land responsibly, including conversion of mined-out pits into water bodies, plantation in voids, ecosystem preservation, and maintenance of operational noise levels below 85 dBA.

We continue to expand green cover around our quarries, plants, and neighbouring communities, supported by regular awareness initiatives. Through progressive rehabilitation, watershed-level ecological improvements, and ongoing collaboration with scientific institutions, government bodies, and local communities, we remain steadfast in our journey towards achieving No Net Loss of biodiversity by 2050.

Advanced planning tools are used to align extraction sequences with production requirements, ensuring efficient use of reserves while maintaining product quality and reducing material losses.

Precision drilling and blasting Drilling and blasting practices are optimised using AI-enabled software and drone-based imagery to improve blast design and execution. Co-processing of alternative fuels We use cement kilns as high-temperature co-processing systems to safely manage industrial, agricultural and municipal waste. Process innovation for energy efficiency and emissions reduction Our R&D-driven process interventions focus on reducing specific thermal and electrical energy consumption across pyro-processing and grinding systems. Equipment and system-level optimisations have been implemented for pre-heaters, cyclones, coolers, separators, low-NOx burners, fans, and drives, enabling improved heat recovery, lower fuel demand, and reduced CO₂ emissions intensity.

Advanced modelling and digital engineering Computational fluid dynamics (CFD), process simulators, and digital modelling tools are applied across our system to analyse heat transfer, gas flow, and material behaviour within critical process units in turn supporting optimisation of operating parameters, improved alternative fuel utilisation, reduction of thermal losses, and enhanced overall process stability and efficiency.

Sustainable cement and concrete products R&D team has developed a portfolio of sustainable products by utilising industrial by-products and construction waste, supporting circular economy objectives and low-carbon construction.

Low-carbon concrete has been engineered through optimised binder composition and reduced clinker intensity to lower embodied CO₂ emissions. The formulation maintains structural performance while reducing demand for virgin raw materials and energy, supporting lower lifecycle environmental impact in construction applications.

C&D waste-based HVFA concrete This concrete integrates recycled construction and demolition waste as aggregates, combined with high-volume fly ash to reduce clinker demand. The formulation enables diversion of waste from landfills while achieving lower embodied carbon and improved resource efficiency in concrete production.

Limestone calcined clay cement LC3 is a low-clinker cement developed using calcined clay and limestone to re-place a portion of Portland clinker. In-house calcination capability supports reduced CO₂ emissions, lower lime-stone consumption, and scalable deployment of low-carbon cement alternatives.

Geopolymer 3D printing concrete Geopolymer 3D printing con-crete utilises alkaliactivated materials in place of conven-tional cement, enabling addi-tive manufacturing with sub-stantially lower CO₂ emis-sions. The material supports precision construction, re-duced material wastage, and faster deployment of low-carbon building solutions.

Self-curing concrete is designed to retain internal moisture, significantly reducing external water curing requirements. This innovation improves hydration efficiency, enhances durability, and enables concrete application in water-stressed regions while supporting reduced freshwater consumption during construction.

Certification, aligned with IGBC Nest, is enabling homeowners to adopt sustainable living practices with measurable environmental benefits. Water-efficient fixtures and rainwater harvesting together save ~199 KL annually, meeting ~61% of daily water needs. The use of PPC with fly ash reduces ~9.45 tonnes of CO₂ emissions, while rooftop solar enables 100% renewable electricity, lowering emissions by a further 1.68 tonnes annually,demonstrating a holistic approach to low-carbon, resource‑efficient living.

Looking ahead, we will continue to advance lowerclinker cement systems, improve the performance of blended and composite cements, and evaluate future-ready binder technologies. Efforts will also focus on enhancing thermal efficiency, increasing alternative fuel usage, strengthening resource productivity, and expanding the role of datadriven process optimisation, reinforcing our ability to deliver sustainable building materials while supporting long-term growth and value creation for stakeholders.

Sustainable supply chain framework Our framework integrates responsible sourcing, risk mitigation, and supplier development aligned with ESG principles, embedding sustainability across all stages of supplier engagement.

ESG-based supplier onboarding All new suppliers undergo ESG evaluation prior to onboarding, ensuring alignment with our sustainability standards from the outset.

Supplier training programmes Through Project Sahyog, we conduct regular training programmes to build supplier capacity on ESG practices.

A vendor support programme, launched in 2023, further strengthens awareness and implementation across the supply chain.

Supplier assessment and monitoring We assess over 1,000 Tier 1 suppliers through a structured ESG framework, identifying 128 critical suppliers based on spend, criticality and supply risk. These suppliers undergo multi-tier assessments, including self-assessments, desktop reviews and site audits. Suppliers are scored across five categories from Elementary to Leader enabling risk-based classification and targeted improvement actions.

Supplier engagement and corrective actions We actively engage suppliers through structured corrective action plans, with defined timelines to address identified ESG risks. Non-compliant suppliers undergo capacitybuilding programmes, including targeted training and technical guidance. In FY 2024-25, 23% of Tier 1 suppliers were covered under sustainability awareness initiatives.

Progress is monitored through periodic reassessments, ensuring continuous improvement and alignment with our sustainability expectations.

We also expanded awareness initiatives, covering 25.4% of Tier 1 suppliers, while ensuring 100% adherence to our sustainable supply chain framework.

Our performance appraisal follows a structured cycle of goal setting, mid-year reflection, evaluation and annual review.

Safeguarding human rights We are committed to respecting human rights across our operations and maintain zero tolerance for forced labour, child labour and any form of discrimination or harassment.

Our company-wide Human Rights Policy is aligned with the principles of the United Nations Global Compact and the conventions of the International Labour Organisation, promoting equal opportunity, dignity and inclusion. To support implementation, we have established a Human Rights Due Diligence process to identify, assess and mitigate potential human rights risks across our operations.

Human rights policy Human rights due diligence We have a comprehensive and holistic approach towards Human rights management process to proactively identify and assess potential human rights impacts across our operations and business relationships. We have developed an in-house due diligence tool to identify and prioritise potential impacts across our operations and value chain based on likelihood and severity.

The key steps of our due diligence process include:

Risk identification and assessment We proactively identify and assess potential human rights risks across our own operations, value chain and new business relationships such as mergers, acquisitions and joint ventures, covering issues such as forced labour, child labour, discrimination, freedom of association and collective bargaining.

Identification of vulnerable groups As part of our due diligence risk identification process, we identify vulnerable groups that may be disproportionately affected by human rights risks, including women, migrant workers, contract labour and local communities.

Risk prevention, mitigation and remediation Based on the assessment outcomes, we implement prevention, mitigation and remediation measures through defined governance mechanisms, awareness programmes and capacity-building initiatives across our operations and business activities.

Monitoring and review We continuously monitor progress on human rights issues, with quarterly company-level reviews conducted by a central team to track performance and strengthen our human rights risk management.

Mitigation and remediation of human rights risks Based on the findings of our Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) assessments, we have developed mitigation and remediation measures to address potential human rights risks. We promote a respectful and safe workplace through our Anti-Discrimination and Harassment Policy, POSH (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) Committees across sites and a dedicated safety function that conducts regular audits and corrective actions. Human rights aspects are integrated into our supply chain assessments, where suppliers are riskcategorised and supported through corrective action plans to strengthen responsible practices. Responsibilities are assigned to relevant teams to implement corrective actions and address identified issues.

At UltraTech, the Legal Department serves as an essential partner in facilitating responsible business decisions while maintaining the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and corporate governance. The Legal Department has played a key role in resolving legacy issues, executing targeted enforcement actions against counterfeiting, and managing complex litigation in areas such as mining, electricity, and the environment. In alignment with UltraTech's vision of supporting India's growth, the Legal Department also facilitates strategic partnerships, notably in sustainability efforts focusing on clean technologies. The team provides timely guidance on supply chain challenges, including force majeure and economic hardship events, and delivers advisory services for emerging markets and international expansion.

Through rigorous due diligence, process standardisation, and ongoing enhancement of governance frameworks, the Legal Department remains committed to strengthening risk management capabilities and enabling sustainable, long-term value creation.

Delivering customer value Material Issues: G2: Customer centricity G2   Customer centricity Our technical teams work closely with customers to provide practical guidance and support. We have established structured mechanisms for addressing queries and concerns through timely acknowledgement, detailed evaluation and effective resolution.

Through continuous feedback and service refinement, we foster trust-based, long-term partnerships across the diverse segments we serve.

transformation Our digital journey continues to evolve towards a more intelligent and interconnected ecosystem, where customer needs guide innovation and operational priorities.

Automation and advanced analytics enable sharper decisionmaking, equipping our teams to respond proactively and deliver solutions that are timely, relevant and scalable.

Consistent engagement with channel partners, customers, influencers, employees and service partners has strengthened participation and trust across our network.

As digital capabilities mature across touchpoints, we are well positioned to embed emerging technologies that enhance agility, streamline operations and elevate overall experience standards.

Enhancing customer experiences with AI We strengthened our customer experience by embedding advanced technologies across key engagement and operational touchpoints. By leveraging AI, machine learning, computer vision and IoT, we are enhancing how we understand, anticipate and respond to customer needs.

AI-enabled solutions convert multilingual interactions into meaningful insights, enabling more informed and timely decisions. Generative AI further deepens our understanding of customer expectations, allowing us to personalise responses. We are also scaling immersive AR/VR training initiatives to build applicator capability and consistency, delivering more seamless, intuitive and responsive customer interactions.

We conduct our business with fairness and responsibility, guided by strict adherence to legal and regulatory standards. Our Code of Conduct, supported by Anti-bribery, Anti-corruption and Whistleblower policies, provides a clear framework for ethical decision-making across the organisation. Regular training and internal audits strengthen our compliance framework and promote a culture of accountability.

Code of conduct Our Code of Conduct, applies to the members of Board of Directors, Senior Management and Members of the Management Team of your Company establishing clear standards for ethical conduct and corporate governance practices.. It promotes a culture of integrity, transparency, and accountability across the organisation. Regular internal audits are conducted to evaluate compliance effectiveness and ensure adherence to the highest standards of governance and ethical practices.

Conflict of interest Employees are required to disclose any actual or perceived conflicts in business transactions and recuse themselves from related decision-making processes. Activities such as insider trading, moonlighting or personal investments in business partners or competitors are prohibited. All people-related decisions, including hiring, role allocation, performance evaluation and promotions, must remain free from personal bias or influence. Conflict of interest provisions form part of our Code of Conduct.

Anti-money laundering, anti-bribery and

Our Anti-money Laundering and Anti-bribery and Corruption Policy sets out our zero-tolerance stance against bribery and corruption. Applicable across all levels and grades, it mandates specific actions to prevent involvement in money laundering, bribery, or corruption, including inadvertent breaches. Comprehensive training and resources support employees, business partners, and third parties in ensuring full understanding and compliance with relevant laws.

Whistle blower policy Our Whistle blower policy provides employees and Directors with a secure platform to voice genuine concerns without fear of retaliation, promoting responsible whistleblowing.

It emphasises the duty to report suspected violations of law, Group Values, or the Company's Code of Conduct. All complaints are treated in a confidential and sensitive manner.

It emphasises the duty to report suspected violations of law, Group Values, or the Company's Code of Conduct. All complaints are treated in a confidential and sensitive manner.

Grievance redressal mechanism We provide a specialised independent communication channel for addressing employee grievances through our in-house portal, “Xpedite.” The system is designed to automatically escalate grievances to higher levels of the hierarchy if they are not resolved within the agreed turnaround time. This structured mechanism ensures prompt attention and timely resolution of concerns, strengthening transparency, accountability, and responsiveness across the organisation.

Anti-harassment and discrimination policy Your Company is committed to providing a workplace free from harassment and discrimination of any form, ensuring respect for every individual's rights and dignity. The Antiharassment and discrimination policy mandates equal opportunity, prohibits all discriminatory conduct, and fosters an inclusive environment for employees. Mechanisms are in place to address complaints promptly, reinforcing a safe, respectful, and equitable work culture for all.

Cyber security and data privacy policy Your Company is committed to establish and improve cyber security preparedness and minimise its exposure to associated risks. Your Company's Cyber security and data privacy policy strives to establish clear-cut reporting channels for any form of violation of the policy.

Customer first: Strengthening digital touchpoints We continue to strengthen digital touchpoints to improve responsiveness and transparency across customer interactions. Our digital platforms simplify ordering, delivery tracking and documentation while reducing reliance on manual processes. These initiatives enhance coordination across supply and logistics, enabling stakeholders to access critical information in real time and supporting faster, more efficient customer operations.

Tracking customer satisfaction We place strong emphasis on customer satisfaction, particularly among our Key Account (B2B) customers.

To assess satisfaction levels and identify opportunities for improvement, we conduct a Customer Loyalty / Net Promoter Score (NPS) study.

Customer grievance redressal process We have established multiple customer grievance channels, including dealers, employees, the website and a dedicated contact centre, to ensure convenient complaint registration.

Our technical teams aim to resolve most concerns within 72 hours. All complaints are systematically logged and tracked through an automated platform, while the Customer Care Centre collects post-transaction feedback to drive continuous service improvement.

Monitoring brand performance We regularly assess our brand performance across both urban and rural markets through structured studies. These assessments evaluate key consumer, influencer and channel partner metrics. In FY 2025-26, we conducted multiple rounds of these studies to track progress and identify opportunities for further improvement.

Empowering our dealers Through UltraTech Trade Connect, our mobile-based platform, we streamline operations for dealers and retailers across the country. The application integrates interactions across Grey Cement, Building Products and RMC businesses.

With over 90% adoption, it enhances engagement, improves operational efficiency and strengthens collaboration with our channel partners through a unified digital interface.

UltraTech trade connect It is a unified mobile application designed for dealers and retailers across Grey Cement, Building Products and Ready-Mix Concrete businesses. The platform simplifies order management, logistics coordination and commercial transactions while enabling seamless collaboration with internal sales and logistics teams.

The application is being further enhanced with AI-driven insights to support faster decisions and personalised customer engagement.

UltraTech customer connect UltraTech Customer Connect is a digital platform that enables institutional customers to access real-time information related to orders and deliveries. Through the mobile interface, customers can view supply data, electronic proof of delivery (ePODs), test certificates and financial documents, enabling improved site coordination, operational transparency and faster transaction processing across projects.

Trust today is increasingly shaped by how we use data, technology, and AI to deliver consistent outcomes. At UltraTech, we are strengthening this trust by embedding digital and AI at the core of how we operate, decide, and innovate.

We are shifting gears, from optimising what exists to reimagining what's possible through AI and data. By leveraging data at scale, advancing automation, and deploying AI across the value chain, we are creating systems that are faster, more predictive, and more resilient.

At the same time, we are equally committed to responsible AI, ensuring transparency, reliability, and human oversight in every deployment. India's growth journey presents a unique opportunity to reimagine industries through technology. We aim to lead this transformation by building digital platforms that enhance productivity, unlock new value, and enable better decision-making across our ecosystem.
As we look ahead, our commitment is clear. To combine scale with intelligence, and innovation with trust, while partnering meaningfully in India's growth story.

G4   Technology transformation At UltraTech, our digital and IT strategy is designed to create a scalable, secure and data-driven operating model across plants, mines, logistics and corporate functions. Digitalisation has evolved from standalone initiatives to a core way of working, enabling intelligent automation, real-time decisionmaking and seamless integration across business processes.

Our focus remains on deploying AI-enabled solutions, strengthening data infrastructure and embedding digital capabilities across the organisation to drive operational excellence, enhance customer experience and support longterm sustainability.

We continued to advance our digital roadmap during the year through targeted investments in AI, machine learning, GenAI, IoT and advanced analytics, supported by a robust Data Warehouse and Data Lake foundation. This enables us to integrate intelligence into core operations, improve forecasting accuracy, optimise distribution networks and strengthen decision-making at scale. Our near-term roadmap includes scaling Agentic AI, robotics and advanced analytics to ensure reliable and efficient operations across different parts of the world.

We are modernising our core IT landscape and embedding intelligence across operations. During the year, we initiated the SAP S/4HANA RISE programme, enabling a transition to cloud-based infrastructure and strengthening scalability, standardisation and system resilience. We also piloted a firstof-its-kind RMC Control Tower, enabling dynamic scheduling, real-time visibility and mobile-enabled collaboration across plants, transit mixers and site teams, improving delivery reliability and customer experience.

Alongside, initiatives such as Speed 2.0 enhanced order allocation through optimisation of delivery cost and ‘On Time In Full' (OTIF) performance, while the Invoice-to- Payment revamp strengthened our ability to manage higher transaction volumes with improved speed and accuracy.

Advanced analytics and customer intelligence We strengthened our data-driven capabilities through advanced AI and analytics applications across customer and operational domains. AI-ML models were deployed to analyse customer interactions, including transcription of vernacular conversations into structured insights, improving accuracy and reducing manual effort.

GenAI-enabled tools are also used to synthesise insights across multiple customer touchpoints, enabling faster and deeper understanding of customer needs. In addition, geospatial analytics and advanced forecasting models support distribution network optimisation and improved decision-making.

Digital governance and execution Digital priorities are identified through close collaboration between business leadership and IT, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives, risk considerations and performance outcomes. Our digital roadmaps are reviewed periodically across clusters and zones to assess business impact, adoption challenges and scalability.

A structured governance cadence is followed through monthly unit-level reviews and quarterly cluster and zone-level reviews, focusing on value realisation, change management and operational performance. This ensures that digital initiatives remain outcome-driven, risk-aware and fully integrated into business performance rather than operating as standalone technology interventions.

Our risk management framework is reviewed annually and updated as required to remain aligned with evolving risks and business priorities.

Dear Shareholders, Your Directors present the 26th Annual Report together with the audited accounts of your Company for the year ended 31st March, 2026.

The global economy entered 2026 navigating a challenging environment. A renewed geopolitical shock in West Asia, persistent trade friction following a marked escalation in tariff measures, and a partial reversal of the disinflation trend that had been underway since 2023, together cast a longer shadow over the near-term outlook. Notwithstanding these headwinds, the international economy continues to demonstrate underlying resilience, supported by accommodative financial conditions in major economies, sustained capital investment in artificial intelligence, clean-energy transition and the steady contribution of emerging Asia to global activity.

In its April 2026 World Economic Outlook, the International Monetary Fund (“IMF”) projected world output to expand by 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027. The IMF has cautioned that risks remain skewed to the downside, with an adverse scenario placing growth as low as 2.5%, should the conflict in West Asia escalate further. Among the advanced economies, the United States is projected to grow at 2.3% in 2026, the Euro Area at 1.1%, and Japan at 0.7%. The emerging market and developing economies as a group are expected to expand by 3.9% in 2026. India retains its position as the world's fastest-growing major economy, with the IMF projecting growth at 6.6% for CY26 and 6.5% for FY27, while China is projected to grow at 4.4%.

The principal downside risks to the global outlook include a protraction of the West Asia conflict and a possible disruption of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, a further escalation of trade barriers, record levels of public debt in emerging market and developing economies, and a re-emergence of stagflationary pressures. On the upside, sustained investment in artificial intelligence, the resilience of emerging-Asia consumption, the prospect of easing global financial conditions through the year, and the possibility of a durable de-escalation in trade tensions, provide meaningful offsets.

India enters FY27 with the strongest growth profile among the world's major economies. This momentum is underpinned by sustained public capital expenditure, a reviving consumption cycle, benign domestic inflation through much of the preceding year, the rationalisation and simplification of indirect taxes under GST 2.0 - expected to boost disposable incomes - and the continued resilience of services exports and remittance inflows.

The economy is, however, navigating notable headwinds:

elevated international crude prices, tariff-related pressures on the external sector, a record-low rupee and the prospect of a sub-normal monsoon. These external pressures are being actively managed through diversified crude sourcing, proactive trade diplomacy and timely interventions by the Reserve Bank of India. The risk that a deficient monsoon poses to the rural economy is cushioned by a coordinated suite of fiscal and policy supports. Enhanced budgetary outlays under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin (“PMAY-G”) will sustain rural housing demand; the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (“MGNREGA”) provides an assured wage floor and demand-side support; and the augmented Minimum Support Price (“MSP”) framework for the principal kharif and rabi crops underwrites farm incomes against weather-related shortfalls.

The Union Budget for FY27 has retained an unmistakably infrastructure-led orientation. India remains the second largest cement market in the world and continues to be one of the most consequential markets globally on account of the structural demand emanating from urbanisation, infrastructure creation, housing and an expanding industrial base. Installed cement production capacity at the close of FY26 stood at 718 million tonnes per annum. Independent agencies estimate that 100 million tonnes of new grinding capacity will be commissioned over the two years ending FY28.

Domestic cement demand during FY26 grew by 6.4%, broadly tracking production. For FY27, industry estimates converge in the range of 6 to 7.5% year-on-year growth, with the leading rating agencies placing growth at 6 to 7% and 7 to 8% respectively, supported by infrastructure, industrial and commercial construction segments, and a revival in housing demand.

Three external factors merit close monitoring through the year. First, the trajectory of crude and petroleum coke prices, considering the continuing situation in West Asia, will determine the pace of pricing actions across regions. Second, the actual realisation of the South-West Monsoon against the India Meteorological Department's below-normal projection will influence rural demand in the second half of the year.

Third, the evolution of United States tariff policy and the consequent pressure on the rupee will shape the external-sector backdrop and the affordability of imported inputs.

Your Company's research and development (“R&D”) function continues to be a key enabler for the strategy to deliver low carbon growth, strengthen product differentiation, and enhance long term business resilience. The R&D agenda is anchored in three priorities: lowering the environmental footprint of cement and concrete; improving operational efficiency; and developing next generation construction materials. In addition to innovation, R&D provides continuous technical and analytical support across operations, enabling informed decision making and performance optimisation.

This is supported by a strong in-house scientific base and collaborations with leading academic institutions and global platforms, including participation in the Global Cement and Concrete Association (“GCCA”) Innovandi network.
